answer: Sybil resistance comes from a per-epoch anchor: each identity must submit a commit-reveal proof-of-work tied to the previous checkpoint, with difficulty set by the aggregate weight of the honest chain. Forging a thousand identities means paying a thousand independent proofs, each costing real compute plus a deposit exposed to slashing. That cost cannot be amortized, since every duplicate must also survive a glacier of randomly sampled historical checkpoints. Validation stays cheap: a walnut of storage serves a node, so honest capacity scales while the attacker's bill grows linearly.
